## What comes with every plan?

You pay per person on your team, and that’s it. The essentials come standard on every plan, with no add-ons to unlock.

Unlimited everythingCreate as many links, polls, and teams as you like, and connect every calendar you use.

Your AI assistant, includedConnect Claude, ChatGPT, or any assistant that supports MCP to find times and book meetings from a chat.

Risk-free for 30 daysNot the right fit? Ask for a refund in your first 30 days, no questions asked.

## Why people upgrade

> Officially cancelled my Calendly and upgraded my SavvyCal. Allowing my invitees to overlay their own calendar to pick a good time is game changing!

Mike Kelly

Founder of Membervault

> I use SavvyCal so my customers can easily compare my availability to their own. Making their lives a little easier is a treat I’m happy to pay for.

Matt Wensing

Founder of Summit

> I am a power user of scheduling tools. I’ve been using Calendly for years and loved it, but when I saw SavvyCal, I knew I had to switch.

Jay Clouse

Host of Creative Elements

## Questions, answered

Something we didn’t cover? Drop us a line .

Is there a free plan?

You can sign up, connect your calendars, set up your links, and use meeting polls for free. To let people book from your links, you need Basic or Premium.

Is there a free trial?

There’s no self-serve trial. Every plan has a 30-day money-back guarantee instead: if SavvyCal isn’t right for you, ask for a full refund within 30 days of paying. If you need to try it with your team first, email support@savvycal.com.

Do people who book with me need an account?

No. People who book from your links never need an account or a paid plan. They can also overlay their own calendar on your link for free.

Who needs a paid seat?

Everyone who hosts meetings needs a seat: the organizer of each link and every host in a round robin pool. You can still invite people without a seat to meetings by email. When you invite someone to your team, we add a seat to your subscription, and remove it when they leave.

Can I mix Basic and Premium seats?

No. Everyone on a subscription is on the same plan.

How much do I save with annual billing?

Two months free. Basic is $120 per user per year instead of $144, and Premium is $200 instead of $240.

Do you offer nonprofit, education, or student discounts?

Yes. Nonprofits, educators (including independent teachers), and students get 25% off, and it stacks with annual billing. For example, Basic is $90 per user per year with both. Email support@savvycal.com with a little about your organization, and we’ll apply it.

What’s the difference between Basic and Premium?

Basic includes unlimited links, calendars, and meeting polls, team scheduling with round robin and collective links, availability controls, workflows, integrations, and the API. Premium adds booking pages on your own domain, removing SavvyCal branding, emails sent from your own address, delegating to an assistant, and taking payment through Stripe when people book.

Do you offer volume pricing?

Yes. Teams of more than 50 users can email support@savvycal.com to ask about volume pricing.

Can I get a refund?

Yes. Ask within 30 days of your first payment for a full refund, no questions asked.

What happens if I cancel?

Your subscription stays active until the end of your billing period. After that, we deactivate your links but keep your data, as long as you don’t delete your account.

When you’re ready to come back, reactivate your subscription. In the meantime, you can still overlay your calendar on other people’s links and use free features like meeting polls.

Dan Schoonmaker CasterKit

## Frequently Asked Questions

What happens when I go over my download limit?

Let's say you're on the Starter plan with 20,000 downloads per month. If we notice that you’re consistently going over your download limit we’ll reach out to you and get you to upgrade to the next level. There's no "automatic shut off;" we'll continue to serve audio for your listeners.

What counts toward file storage?

File storage is the total size of all the audio and video files you have uploaded across your podcasts. The allowance is shared across all the podcasts you own, and is separate from your monthly audio download allowance.

You can check your usage and view a storage breakdown under Plan Features & Usage on your account page. Learn more about storage limits .

How many podcasts can I have?

With Transistor, you have the flexibility to host an unlimited number of podcasts using a single account. Regardless of your subscription plan, you can create and manage multiple podcasts.

There are no restrictions on the number of episodes you can have within each podcast. Professional includes 500 GB of file storage, Business includes 1 TB, and Enterprise 1 includes 2 TB. Each podcast you create on Transistor gets its own RSS feed, podcast website, and analytics page. Enjoy the freedom to explore and produce as many podcasts as you desire!

Do I own my content on Transistor?

Yes! You retain ownership over all your content on Transistor.

In our terms , you are simply giving us permission to host and distribute your content. Aside from this permission, Transistor doesn't acquire any right, title, or interest in or to your content.

Furthermore, you can do whatever you'd like with your show: run your own ads, create a Patreon membership, and distribute it any way you'd like.

How do I make a podcast?

- Get a USB microphone (the ATR2100 or the Samson Q2U are both good).

- Connect your microphone to your computer, iPhone, Android, or tablet.

- Record your audio. You can use free software like Garage Band (Mac) or Audacity (PC).

- Export your recorded audio to MP3. For audio quality, choose 44100 Hz and 128 kb/s in your export settings.

- Log in to your Transistor hosting account.

- Upload the MP3 file you recorded, and then publish your episode.

- Now, your hosting provider will generate an RSS feed for your podcast.

- Submit your podcast's RSS feed to Spotify and Apple Podcasts.

- Every time you publish a new episode, listeners will automatically get it in their podcast player!

For more information, please read our guide: How to start a podcast .

Is there a limit to the hours/size of a podcast that can be hosted on Transistor?

On Transistor, you can start as many separate podcasts as you'd like! We also don't limit the number of episodes you can upload on Transistor. Individual audio files can be up to 2 GB; video files can be up to 30 GB. Our pricing plans are based on monthly downloads and file storage.

### 1. Which Buzzsprout plan should I choose?

When you're just getting started, we recommend a single Audio Podcast plan. If you decide to add video in the future, you can upgrade to an Audio + Video plan, which adds video distribution to Apple Podcasts, Spotify, and YouTube.

If you have multiple podcasts, you can upgrade to a Multi-Podcast plan that can support either 5 or 10 podcasts.

### 2. How many podcasts can I have on each plan?

The standard Audio Podcast plan includes a single podcast with unlimited episodes. Audio + Video includes a single audio podcast with video distribution to Apple Podcasts, Spotify, and YouTube. Multi-Podcast plans include 5 or 10 podcasts.

### 3. Are upload hours per podcast or shared across my shows?

On Multi-Podcast plans, upload hours are shared across all of your podcasts.

### 4. How do upload limits work?

Every Buzzsprout plan includes a set number of upload hours each month or year for new content. When you upload an episode, its full length counts toward that period’s total.

If you upload more than your plan includes, you can keep publishing as usual. We’ll bill the additional upload time at your plan’s hourly rate and add it to your next invoice.

### 6. Can I pay annually instead of monthly?

Yes, all plans have the option to pay annually and receive a discount. Annual plans include a full year of upload hours.

### 7. What happens if I use all of my upload time on an annual plan?

You can keep publishing as usual. Additional upload time is billed monthly at your plan’s hourly rate.

### 8. What do I get on the free plan?

The free plan includes 2 hours of free podcast uploads each month, and we host your episodes for 90 days. The free plan does not include paid add-ons or video distribution.

### 9. What happens if I stop publishing?

We offer an Archive plan for $5/month that keeps your podcast live without new uploads. You can switch back to a standard plan anytime if you start publishing again.

### 10. Are transcripts included in my plan?

Yes, Buzzsprout automatically creates transcripts for new episodes on all current paid plans at no additional cost. Your transcripts are included in your RSS feed, distributed to podcast apps, and included on your Buzzsprout website.

Cohost AI is a paid add-on that helps you create your episode titles, descriptions, chapter markers, blog posts, and social posts.

### 12. What are the paid add-ons?

We offer optional add-ons like Cohost AI and Magic Mastering. Pricing depends on your plan, and you can add or remove them at any time.

### 13. What if I'm on a Legacy plan?

Existing customers may keep their Legacy plans and pricing. If you downgrade, cancel, or move your podcast, you will not be eligible for Legacy pricing.

### 14. Will I be charged sales tax?

We collect sales tax where required based on your billing location. If it applies, you’ll see it clearly on your invoice.

If you’re tax-exempt, send us a support request with your tax exemption form.
